title: Marvell to buy Lumentum for $115B in AI optical-connectivity mega-deal
subtitle: The all-stock transaction values Lumentum at $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium, and combines Marvell's electrical silicon with Lumentum's lasers, optical components, and MEMS-based optical circuit switching. The market punished both stocks on announcement.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Marvell Technology announced on November 2 that it will acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at about $115 billion including debt, with closing expected in the first half of 2028. Lumentum shareholders would receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share — roughly $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's last unaffected close. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy will lead the combined company, with Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston joining the board. The strategic case is vertical integration of the optical interconnect stack: Marvell has supplied the electrical silicon — DSPs, SerDes, retimers — that lives at the edges of optical links, while Lumentum contributes the lasers, optical components, and MEMS-based optical circuit switching that move the photons themselves. Marvell projects the combined total addressable market at roughly $550 billion.

Markets were unkind. Marvell shares dropped about 13% on the announcement; Lumentum fell nearly 19%. The sell-off reflects three anxieties — the 23.9% premium is high by chip-industry standards, the two-year close exposes the deal to antitrust and macro risk, and some analysts question whether Marvell's integration record justifies a transaction this large. That said, the underlying thesis — that AI compute buildouts will shift aggressively from copper to optical interconnects — is the near-consensus view across hyperscalers, and ownership of both halves of the optical stack is a credible moat if the integration works.

The deal sits inside a broader pattern of AI-era chip consolidation. ON Semiconductor's recent $600M acquisition of Ferric for AI power delivery, Analog Devices' closing of its Alif Semiconductor purchase, and ongoing rumors about further packaging and interconnect deals all point the same way: the AI infrastructure stack is being rolled up by acquirers trying to own vertical slices across compute, memory, power, and interconnect. The $115B headline makes the Marvell–Lumentum transaction the largest of these so far, and if it closes, it reshapes who negotiates with Nvidia, AMD, and the hyperscalers on behalf of the optical side of the system.

A takeaway for learners: the compute stack is more than the GPU. If you are thinking about where AI value accrues over the next five years, the parts least visible in press releases — interconnects, power delivery, cooling, networking — are where margin is now moving, because the GPU itself is scarce, standardized, and sold through a small number of hands. Study the system, not just the chip. The companies that supply what sits around the GPU are often the ones with the most durable pricing power, which is why deals like this one carry the price tags they do.
